fresh_checks: Gauduchon quotient denominator scales as r^(n-1); in dimension1 it is integral mu=1. Stokes makes all pseudoeffective quotients nonnegative; fixed testing gives finiteness, infimum linearity gives concavity and smooth upper semicontinuity.

Smooth positive representatives allow application of the complete Chapter9 smooth equation. Pointwise trace/n arithmetic--geometric mean gives the exact root scalar, with no missing n factor. Equality makes the minimizing metric conformal to the solution; Gauduchon uniqueness fixes its ray. Curve scalars follow by integration.

A strict positive current theta-delta h makes lambda positive by monotonicity; the converse bigness statement remains explicitly open. Equality of concavity makes one metric minimize both endpoints, whose fixed-mu volume forms give constant proportionality. The curve case follows from zero-integral Green solvability.

The fixed positive representative and earlier smooth implicit-function result give finite-family smoothness. Differentiating Omega^n=lambda^n mu and Gauduchon Stokes give the derivative denominator exactly lambda^(n-1) integral e^((n-1)g)mu.

Second differentiation at the fixed adjoint probability removes the second potential derivative without differentiating the measure. Constant trace A=n dotlambda/lambda yields the two Hessian identities. Positive adjoint density makes their kernels radial-plus-ddc and exactly dd-c respectively, including dimension1.
The linearized solution is linear in the direction; polarization gives a positive definite form on the smooth dd-c quotient. Smooth representative changes leave Omega and the bilinear form unchanged.

The derivative functional on all smooth forms determines Xi. Its unique positive root has D_mu=1 by homogeneity; combining its direction and lambda reconstructs Omega. Every Gauduchon ray gives a normalized class via its fixed-mu conformal metric. Dimension1 retains the separate scalar-integral statement.

P intersects an injective finite-dimensional direction space in an open convex cone. Euler's identity and twice-differentiated homogeneity make log lambda radial unit length and orthogonal to its level set. Product path length gives the exact squared distance formula and completeness equivalence; zero/infinite lambda has infinite length.

P1 product intersection numbers give lambda=sqrt(2ab), Hessian half squared logarithmic differentials, distinct equal-volume-profile classes and the intrinsic complete Euclidean metric. Blowup incidence embedding and curve integrals give a>b>0; intersections give sqrt(a^2-b^2), with r/s coordinates and Euclidean closed-half-plane completion at positive-volume nef boundary.

Trace-normalized current matrix density has trace n and determinant root at most1. Cofactor algebra and homogeneity recover the smooth denominator. The positive-matrix determinant dual, epsilon inverse test and bound1+epsilon prove the pointwise infimum formula.

For fixed epsilon the measurable positive matrix field has uniform spectral bounds; Lusin/extension/partition approximation and determinant normalization give continuous tests in L1 of the trace measure. The infimum representation proves concavity and weak upper semicontinuity on the bounded positive-current set, without requiring smooth current approximation.

Weak-current compactness gives attained positive maximum. A rescaled smooth solution supplies the determinant dual test, Stokes fixes the value, and equality forces the current into one conformal matrix direction. The scalar elliptic adjoint equation makes its positive distribution smooth and constant for the Gauduchon metric, giving unique normalized smooth maximizer.

Uniform approximation of continuous F and multiplicative bounds transport the smooth scalar formula to continuous data and preserve equality with the smooth supremum. The approximation is of F, not of every current.

Upper semicontinuity for F+n log(1 plus/minus epsilon h), equal limiting total masses and both signs give weighted-measure continuity for near maximizers. Determinant concavity at common coefficient measure becomes affine equality on maximizers.

Jensen gives the supporting probability inequality with the correct negative sign. Uniform Taylor expansion and near-maximizer compactness give right derivative minus maximal probability pairing; compact convex separation identifies all supports. Absolute continuity here is of determinant-weighted measures, not entire currents. Further conformal weak-power representation remains a question.

Equation lower coefficient bounds and trace duality give uniform L^q determinant density for1<q<n/(n-1). Positive f0 makes determinant vanish on singular trace parts. Endpoint duality uses lower mass; the later mass-extrema theorem was read completely and derives the reverse smooth tests from exact-background regularization and bounded continuity without using the endpoint theorem. The endpoint exponent cancels the expressing-volume density change.

Bounded F support densities get the stated exp(2R/n)/M(0) bound. Hopf trace normalization with omega^3/6 gives constant determinant density6^(-1/3), compatible with infinite upper mass and lower mass6. Complete concentration and vanishing-lower-mass proofs confirm that smooth maximal value does not control higher moments and all-current endpoint failure does not settle a restricted maximizing family.

Subcritical L^r estimates with r>n make bounded measurable weights uniform limits of smooth positive weights. The general root supremum interchanges two suprema only; it does not imply attainment. Vanishing root tails give uniform upper-semicontinuous approximation, compact attainment and uniform integrability by the two-term tail/small-set estimate.

Uniform integrability is equivalent to vanishing root tails. Bounded multiplicative perturbations tending in measure give root-norm continuity on the order interval. Failure chooses smooth tests detecting tails, compact high-weight sets and shrinking smooth cutoffs; one fixed amplitude makes the root norm exceed twice its original value while densities converge in L1, giving the threshold factor2^(-n).

A uniformly integrable selected maximizing sequence controls its truncation errors. Bounded-weight upper semicontinuity gives its limiting maximal value; positive measure domination and equal mass identify all weighted-measure limits. This is weaker than uniform tails for all currents.

For integrable f with root in D0, order-ideal bounds keep logarithmic thresholds finite. Hölder gives log-convex root supremum and concavity of B; translation and Lipschitz rules follow from homogeneity. The weighted-maximizer Taylor/separation argument gives both one-sided derivatives, compact affine support probabilities, and uniform integrability under bounded F.

Smooth test trace saturation has positive error mass1-b^(1/n)D_p(T), independent of the subsolution. At a smooth maximizing sequence it vanishes in total variation uniformly. Under tails, the selected current limit identifies the weighted probability. The book does not define a product with an arbitrary singular limiting test.

A smooth strictly positive maximizing test annihilates the trace error. Its trace controls all current coefficient measures by an L^n density. Countably many locally constant positive Hermitian tests give the determinant lower bound simultaneously almost everywhere; equality with the given trace forces A=a gamma, including a=0. Only after the earlier smooth-conformal-current lemma makes a/u smooth is its nonlinear top power used. Existence uses the previously fully reviewed threshold subsolution result; differences are constant.

The smooth test makes the density smooth nonnegative; finite-p theory and unique threshold clusters give uniform normalized exponential convergence. In a closed positive background the equation da=-a C prevents zeros along paths, giving strict positivity. The earlier all-L1 Kähler scalar formula was additionally checked in section_individual_density_subsolutions.tex lines77–107, using closed mass, smooth truncations and comparison.

The nonclosed example takes a=L chi vanishing on a small open set and omega=a gamma-ddc psi. The local negative Hessian and global large L give a Hermitian form. Its smooth solution has density a^n gamma^n/dV; the Gauduchon quotient gives threshold1. If omega were closed, the preceding characterization would contradict its zeros. Dimension1 is excluded from this regularity implication: its unique constant normalized Gauduchon current maximizes even nonsmooth L1 densities.

For a smooth semipositive maximizer positive outside a proper analytic set, convex positive regularizations give uniform determinant convergence and full trace equality. Local positive-root rigidity gives smoothness and the equation off that set; both nonpluripolar and density measures vanish on it, giving finite global mass. Taking a maximum and the earlier ordered analytic rigidity lemma forces constant-difference uniqueness.

Its determinant-weighted probability has L^n density; uniform qpsh moment bounds and Hölder give a uniform negative normalized-potential moment. Trace inequality and Jensen give c_lambda<=b exp(C lambda); the greatest exponential barrier gives c_lambda>=b and v_lambda>=u0-C. Normalized compactness and the earlier greatest-normalized-threshold result identify every L1 cluster with u0. Capacity and stronger norm limits are still pending.

Capacity uses the genuine P_delta-omega(u0) hypothesis, a common u0-C barrier, dominated fixed-L1-density self-error, and the previously reviewed lower-barrier criterion. Lp yields bounded/continuous threshold solution and full uniform exponential convergence by uniqueness. Trace-rate mass identity R=N-P gives total variation at most 2N and N at most C lambda/n.

Eigenvalue square-root Cauchy inequalities bound the absolutely continuous coefficient error by 2n sqrt(s(s-alpha)); integration and singular trace control give local O(sqrt(lambda)), only away from Z. Divisor-independence uses a small Bott-Chern-zero signed divisor perturbation, nonclosed residual positivity, extension of the equation across a pluripolar set, and semi-positive threshold uniqueness. Positive divisor coefficients only are constrained.

The squared-coordinate projective map gives A=(1/2)F*omega, global potential, integral A^n=1, explicit density with |z_i|^2 zeros and nonsmooth nth root, and semi-positive cofactor maximizer. Closed mass bound proves threshold one. Near-maximal Gauduchon tests plus uniform negative-psh moments give Jensen scalar bound and the common greatest-threshold barrier. Capacity needs the additional delta-envelope; only subsequential exact solutions are asserted.

Uniform entropy and exponential integrability give the psh moment bound using truncated potentials and Gibbs entropy; t log t lower bound gives root-tail uniform integrability and selected weak attainment. Portmanteau passes negative-psh moments. No current regularity follows. Nef regularization and commuting infima give h-independent limiting lambda; zero attained degree implies zero positive current and a smooth global ddC potential.

Closed-nef core subtraction is constrained by a curve with zero alpha and B degree. Positive endpoint core volume gives a positive variational endpoint; FTC expresses the finite improper subtraction cost. Two initial metric bounds and weak ddC B bounds with closed mixed powers give the stated oscillation estimate. Bigness invokes the stated closed-nef-big external result; nonclosed torsion remains fixed.

Mixed nef intersections give the sufficient Morse estimate, not a necessary condition. On the incidence blowup L^2=LM=1, M^2=0, endpoint lower bound 3/2, initial 11/sqrt(8), and an explicit exceptional-divisor big current all agree; the Morse bound is negative. Changing probability volume changes lambda by inverse denominator factors. The scalar profile ranges through precisely all smooth positive-potential raw masses.

Exact-background bounded decreasing regularization identifies smooth and bounded mass extrema. This independently resolves the earlier endpoint determinant-bound dependency without circularity. The double infimum and optimal volume form gamma^n/int gamma^n give the lower-mass Gauduchon formula. Smooth minimum attainment is equivalent to an attained degree quotient and a Gauduchon critical representative. Nef affine extension only identifies the specified perturbative limit, not every singular lower-volume definition.

Oscillatory local gradient tests detect the weak sign of an (n-1,n-1) form. First and second mass variations give ddC Omega^(n-1)=0 and the stated sign of ddC Omega^(n-2). In dimension three all higher terms are exact, so the quadratic formula is globally sufficient; higher dimension is only a necessary-condition statement.

Hopf Gauduchon minimum and unbounded upper mass are compatible. A metric with ddC g=ddC g^2=0 has all powers ddC-closed, so domination h>=c g yields the lower-mass and critical determinant norm bounds. Product elliptic concentration has trace normalization one, determinant k=V^(-1/n) f^((n-1)/n), constant critical norm, and a mean-zero first-factor Poisson potential with correct 4pi Laplacian normalization.

Closed power-difference identity gives all claimed Bott-Chern/Aeppli classes, including n=2. Jensen plus t=1/log(1/epsilon) yields a maximizing sequence while all supercritical norms diverge. Elliptic quotient is free and proper with compact strip; the metric has complementary horizontal and vertical kernels. Local smooth bump and concentration definitions are well posed.

Lamari and normalized compactness would turn a bounded trace-concentration subsequence into a potential with Lelong number >=1 along a local hypersurface. Siu analyticity plus deck-translated hyperplanes and their accumulation force an analytic subset to contain an open set, a contradiction. Local translations commute with the deck group, preserve ddC-closure, have uniform degree bound, and their strictly positive kernel spreads the large trace across V_j. Curve-average proof remains unread after its statement.

Curve matrices have determinant a-bu bounded below by 5/8, so the projective lines stay in the quotient domain and inject after the deck quotient. The evaluation map is a holomorphic submersion at finite and infinite base points. Compact parameter support gives smooth positive closed averages and bounded area. For fixed j, solving tau and b in the local chart proves C-infinity approximate-identity convergence; no uniform j claim. Horizontal covectors dy-a dx span the dual. The cofactor identity Q=2 det(H) H^-1 gives root density (3/sqrt(2))sqrt(det Q); its Schur complement gives delta^-2 sqrt(J) on a region of volume proportional to delta^2.

Choose epsilon_j separately after fixing j. Root volume R_j diverges while every h-degree stays bounded. Testing the smooth equation with eta_j gives mass at most P_j^3/R_j^2. Split product expansions propagate zero lower mass in all dimensions >=3; metric comparison and the independent Hopf upper-mass degeneration give simultaneous failures in dimensions >=6. The fixed-density smooth scalar remains positive. Endpoint failure concerns the full normalized current family, not the maximizing subset.

For the quotient metric ddC t=beta-alpha, dD=-dt wedge B, ddC D=-B^2=2 alpha beta, and d omega^2=0. Fiber period 2pi gives integral D=4pi and total mass 24pi. Threefold variation gives mass 24pi minus 6 times vertical Dirichlet energy. For u=f(t)+base potential, positivity forces |fprime|<1 and fsecond>-1. The mean-zero slope estimate integral p^2<L-4/3 proves the strict mass gap 8.

Periodic smoothing of the extremal piecewise slope preserves mean zero and gives strict positivity after scaling, proving sharpness of gap 8. The exact nonzero semipositive alpha beta excludes both pluriclosed metrics and closed Kähler currents by Stokes. Logarithmic degeneration orders are between zero and n and independent of smooth probability measure, direction, smooth gauge, and positive scaling; reversing inequalities after division by log epsilon is essential.

Closed nef Kähler degeneration is the leading nonzero mixed intersection coefficient, hence n minus numerical dimension. Hopf alpha perturbation has order one while every positive perturbation still has infinite upper mass. The elliptic surface determinant can be made constant by a mean-zero base Poisson correction, with c positive by the strict Schur complement.

Dividing the elliptic solution form by g makes a smooth Gauduchon test attaining equality. Finite zeros yield the constants pi log(1/epsilon) and pi integral (1+t^m)^-1; flat rank-one coefficients are smooth by exponential decay of all derivatives. Splitting harmonic-mean integrals at L gives log I=L-log L+O(1) and log K=L-P(L)+O(log L), hence slope 1+p(L), including unequal and irrational orders.

Smooth-center blowup relative curvature is positive on the kernel of the pulled-back metric; a sufficiently large pullback coefficient makes a global positive metric. Iteration retains an effective exceptional divisor. Domination by analytic elimination of indeterminacy is explicitly a classical input. Exceptional divisor pairing with pulled-back (n-1,n-1) tests vanishes by rank, producing a uniform upstairs/downstairs metric pairing. Nef pullback and regularized cofactor tests give the numerator comparison.

Cofactor determinant extends continuously on semidefinite matrices and dominated convergence justifies the denominator limit across the exceptional locus. Degree-one change of variables and mu_Y>=c pi*mu_X give the full volume comparison and the correctly reversed order inequalities. Incidence blowup radial endpoint slopes give total mass (x+y)^m-y^m and the exact reference cumulative distributions.

The product solution has constant total density and its g-scaled (n-1)-power is closed: the first term is top degree on the base and the second is closed. The beta-function singular integral gives downstairs order max(p-m/k,0) and upstairs p-1/k, including logarithmic equality and both quoted constants. Positive-current subtraction compares every quotient only when the residual is still smooth nef.

Coordinate divisor examples realize all integer residual jumps; elliptic examples realize fractional jumps and destroy existence of a common order. Blowing up two points gives a pseudoeffective residual with negative line intersection, hence not nef. Perturbative minimal multiplicities vanish for nef backgrounds, while the unique actual ruled-surface boundary current is divisorial and removal changes order one to two. Formal qu:nef-degeneration-exponent remains open.

Open-cone/affine-space Hahn-Banach separation yields a nonzero positive order-zero ddC-closed current; compact normalized tests give the exact smooth-positivity threshold and the nef boundary. A positive nef volume forces an annihilating current determinant measure to vanish via epsilon testing, without analytic support claims. Chern-Ricci and scalar-flow 2pi normalization match.

The affine positive reference path and fixed adjusted volume form recover the metric flow. Two exact time-dependent maximum-principle quantities bound dot u up to a hypothetical earlier maximal time. The trace estimate retains dot g, cancels the Laplacian of dot u, and uses the torsion correction plus inverse-shifted u to bound inverse trace, then trace by determinant. Chain-rule factors and the n=1 branch agree.

Uniform matrix bounds allow a concave uniformly elliptic real extension and the stated classical parabolic Evans-Krylov/Schauder continuation. This is an external regularity input, not an independent reproof. Compact current tests compute lifetime 1/b and a nef annihilator at finite time; the text does not infer localization or convergence of singularities. Divisor feasibility begins with legitimate nonclosed divisorial removal.

Divisor feasibility is equivalent to residual pseudoeffectivity and all nonnegative Gauduchon degrees, including a scalar Green proof on curves. The endpoint exists by non-strict Lamari inequalities; bounded remainder is not implied. When residual has a smooth positive representative, subtracting the divisor reduces every threshold subsolution to the strictly smooth dual-rigidity equation. Scalar uniqueness for ordinary bounded residuals uses strict domination, including scalar zero.

Residual root volume derivative is negative divisor degree over the optimizing denominator. Finite coefficient families are smooth in the open positive cone with fixed mean normalization; fixed-divisor L1 and capacity convergence and exact total variation follow. Pullback coefficients equal specified orders on every model. Ideals may jump at an integer despite coefficient convergence, as the one-variable floor integral proves.

On the Hopf example the Gauduchon quotient (1+2t)/(2t) gives threshold one. Residual volumes are 6(1-a)^2; endpoint zeta perturbations have 6 epsilon^2(1+epsilon), hence zero nef volume and zero extended divisor measure. Scaling the known smooth Hopf potentials gives unbounded upper mass for every positive residual.

The two prose summaries now say every nonzero finite non-pluripolar measure, matching the actual Chapter13 corollary. The zero measure is not included in that universal solvability statement. All equation statements, proofs, formulas and formal questions are unchanged.

Divisor feasibility gives a positive residual current; smooth remainder, bounded type and finite parameter convergence retain their explicit positive-cone hypotheses.
